spatial_claims.claim: AB is a straight line cut at random at point C; AB is produced to D so that BD = BC; points are collinear in order A-C-B-D
B is the midpoint of CD since CB = BD
Line AD is cut at C into segments AC and CD (C lies between A and D)
Line CD is cut at B into segments CB and BD (B lies between C and D)
CD is composed of CB and BD (segment decomposition)
Line AB is cut at C (C lies between A and B)

configuration_map: Single straight line with points in order A, C, B, D. C is between A and B (the random cut point). D is beyond B with BD = BC. B is the midpoint of segment CD. All reasoning operates on this collinear configuration with no auxiliary points off the line.
pass_reason: All spatial claims involve collinear point ordering on a single straight line (A-C-B-D) and are mutually consistent throughout the proof. The proof is essentially algebraic manipulation of area identities (Propositions 2.1, 2.3, 2.4) with no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, and no complex spatial configurations that could generate contradictions.
